The story is a cohesive and tightly woven dialogue where every detail serves the central theme of betrayal and moving on. The beginning establishes the past relationship and the Changes that have occurred over six months (symbolized by the changed coffee order and Marie's haircut). The middle logically reveals the source of the conflict—Lukas betraying Marie for a promotion at work. This leads naturally to the end, where Lukas attempts to reconnect over a box of old books, giving Marie the final, satisfying opportunity to reject him and leave the past (and the untouched coffee) behind. Every action and line of dialogue propels this single narrative arc forward without any disjointed or unnecessary elements.
